correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=2, each t_i>0 and B>0, articulation-point resistance additivity yields the exact independent-petal objective before any symmetrization. Trace-inverse strict convexity of the connected Laplacian, coupled with injective edge coordinates, proves global uniqueness. Within each triangle the two spoke prices coincide, so its leaf-swap automorphism forces equality of their optimal weights. Explicit differentiation of F_t(r) gives a strictly increasing derivative numerator and exactly one local optimum, even at the price boundary; the interior radical and boundary formula agree. Cauchy-Schwarz distributes the remaining budgets with a unique equality case. The actual standalone program reproduced 549 exact symbolic, exact rational and numerical checks, including full weighted Laplacian calculations and asymmetrical competitors. The analytic proof, not finite trials, verifies the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The claimed contribution is the complete mixed-price design law for arbitrarily many independently priced triangular petals: unique conductance weights, closed radical objective, budget shares and independent activation patterns. General convex/KKT theory and a tree-plus-optional-chord deletion criterion cover the abstract optimization framework and the zero-chord threshold, respectively; neither produces the mixed-regime conductance formula and all-petal budget allocation as a stated result. The relevant Ghosh-Boyd-Saberi full text, current broad augmentation paper, and closest same-topology bibliography were compared. Full access to the Sardar-Xu same-topology article was unavailable; its accessible abstract specifies unit resistors. Residual risks are recorded.
residual_risks: Sardar and Xu full text could not be inspected; assessment of its absence of priced optimization relies on the explicit unit-weight abstract, not invented whole-document coverage.
The general tree-with-chords deletion criterion already implies the high-price threshold; that boundary is not itself an originality claim.
No search of indexed literature proves absence of an unindexed specialized closed-form conductance allocation theorem.
General first-order semidefinite programs subsume the objective numerically, although they do not state or supply the closed optimizer classification.

value.rationale: The complete, explicitly priced optimization is a naturally motivated infinite family: m independently priced local cycles meet at one cut vertex and compete for the same conductance budget. Unlike an isolated triangle or a trivial reparametrization of a known deletion test, the result settles every mixed support pattern and computes exact unique weights and objective for all independent price vectors. Its provable square-root budget coupling and compensatory ordering are concrete design consequences that are neither furnished by generic convexity nor a previously determined high-price cutoff. The result deliberately claims a complete natural classification, not arbitrary general cactus networks or a general optimization framework.
